skill.name: backend-models
skill.description: Guides AI coding agents when creating or editing Laravel Eloquent models, relationships, casts, timestamps, validation logic, factories, and seeders.
skill.summary: Guides AI agents to create and review Laravel Eloquent backend models with consistent ORM conventions.

remediation.suggestion: Bundle the referenced backend model standards inside the skill package or replace the link with a package-local path that does not use ../ segments.

content.value_statement: Database model work can drift from project standards and create inconsistent relationships or casts. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create Eloquent models with clear attributes, constraints, factories, and seeders.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation and editing of model files in app/Models/ and similar directories.
Covers Eloquent relationships such as hasMany, belongsTo, belongsToMany, hasOne, and morphTo.
Addresses model casts, fillable attributes, hidden attributes, timestamps, scopes, accessors, and mutators.
Supports model validation logic, database constraints, indexes, foreign keys, and ORM configuration.
Provides guidance for model factories and seeders that use backend models.
limitations: The detailed model standards are referenced through a separate relative documentation link.
It is focused on Laravel Eloquent and may need adaptation for other ORM frameworks.
It does not run migrations, framework commands, or database checks by itself.
It does not replace review of project-specific schema and business rules.

use_cases.title: Create New Models
use_cases.description: Define an Eloquent model with relationships, casts, timestamps, and fillable attributes that match project conventions.

use_cases.title: Review Model Changes
use_cases.description: Check model edits for naming, relationships, scopes, mutators, and validation boundaries before merge.

use_cases.title: Prepare Test Data Models
use_cases.description: Shape factories and seeders that use models consistently for tests and local data setup.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new model file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-models skill to create an Eloquent model for [entity]. Include fillable fields, casts, timestamps, and the table name if needed.

prompt_templates.title: Add Relationships
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate update to connect existing models.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-models skill to update [model] with relationships to [models]. Explain the relationship type and foreign key assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Review Model Layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-models skill to audit the models in [path]. Check casts, fillable fields, hidden attributes, scopes, accessors, mutators, and validation logic.

prompt_templates.title: Design Model Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a new backend feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-models skill to propose a model design for [feature]. Include relationships, constraints, indexes, factories, seeders, and risks.

output_examples.input: Create a model plan for a Post entity with authors and comments.
output_examples.output: A concise model plan covering attributes, casts, User and Comment relationships, timestamps, and factory and seeder notes.

output_examples.input: Review the Order model before merging a checkout feature.
output_examples.output: A review summary that flags relationship assumptions, mass assignment concerns, missing casts, and schema checks to confirm.

output_examples.input: Design model support for a subscription feature.
output_examples.output: A backend model outline with entities, relationship types, constraints, indexes, test data needs, and open implementation questions.

best_practices: Keep model responsibilities focused on relationships, casts, scopes, and attribute transformations.
Confirm table names, keys, indexes, and constraints before generating model changes.
Use factories and seeders to validate relationships with realistic test data.
anti_patterns: Putting request validation or controller workflow logic directly in models.
Creating relationships without confirming foreign key names or cascade behavior.
Adding fillable or hidden attributes without checking mass assignment and privacy effects.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Laravel Eloquent model work, including relationships, casts, factories, seeders, and model configuration.

faq.question: Can it create database migrations?
faq.answer: It can help reason about constraints and indexes, but the skill is focused on model files and ORM configuration.

faq.question: Does it cover testing data?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for model factories and seeders used in testing or local data setup.

faq.question: Can Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I provide in a prompt?
faq.answer: Provide the entity name, expected fields, relationships, table assumptions, and any project-specific constraints.

faq.question: Is the skill self-contained?
faq.answer: Not fully. It points to a separate backend model standards document through a relative link.
